# TheLis3k -- Ksawery

> Full-stack developer who ships end to end -- from product framing and architecture
> down to the last pixel. Language-agnostic by choice: picks the right stack for the
> problem instead of forcing the problem into a familiar stack.

## Snapshot

- **Role:** Full-stack developer, automation engineer, product-minded builder, mentor
- **Currently:** Part-time IT student at PJATK; developer at Talentech on the product **Weekli**
- **Operating principle:** Clean architecture, SOLID, and shipping real value are the
  baseline -- not the goal. Kaizen: leave every system better than he found it.
- **People instinct:** Builds up the people around him as naturally as he builds software --
  workshops, pre-exam lectures, onboarding, conflict resolution, translating the
  incomprehensible into the obvious.

## Why he's worth a conversation

He sits in the rare overlap between four roles most people only do one of:

**As an engineer** -- Builds production systems solo, across the whole stack: React/Angular
frontends, Spring Boot and NestJS backends, PostgreSQL/MongoDB data layers, Docker, CI, and
the Bash/Playwright glue in between. Auth done right (JWT with rotating refresh tokens,
invitation-based onboarding), not auth done "good enough." Picks up new languages and
frameworks fast because he learns the underlying model, not just the syntax.

**As a tech lead** -- Thinks in systems, not tickets. At Talentech he architects automation
for client migrations, eliminates entire categories of manual work, and drives integrations
others wrote off as "too complex to automate." Translates fuzzy business needs into concrete
technical designs, and translates technical trade-offs back into plain language stakeholders
can actually decide on. Writes code that the *next* developer can read.

**As a product manager** -- Builds things because they should exist, then makes them usable.
Mobile-first, bilingual UX, real onboarding flows, design-agency finish on a one-person
budget. He doesn't just ask "can we build it?" -- he asks "should we, and what's the smallest
version that delivers the value?" Product analytics and business-data instincts inform what
gets built, not just how.

**As a mentor and leader** -- Led a team of up to 12 people at AmRest: delegated, coached,
resolved conflicts, introduced new procedures, and onboarded new staff. At Plac Zabaw Pingwiny
managed up to 10 people, trained them on all attractions, resolved employee disputes, and kept
the venue running smoothly through busy seasons. At Talentech ran an internal Agentic AI
workshop for the engineering team (Skills, Rules, Sub-Agents, Multi-Repo) and drove the team's
adoption of AI tooling. At PJATK organises pre-exam study sessions for classmates, participates
in budget planning on the student council, runs AI-cost and AI-tooling discussions in the
PJATK{AI} science club, and helps non-technical colleagues understand what AI agents actually
do and what they cost. He doesn't just know things -- he makes sure the people around him know
them too.

## Skills

**Tech:** JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Dart, Flutter, C#, .NET, React, Angular, Spring Boot,
NestJS, SvelteKit, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Drizzle ORM, Docker, Linux, Bash, Playwright,
Cypress, Python, Automated Testing, E2E Testing, CI/CD, Azure DevOps, Git, Vite,
Product Analytics, Business Data Collection, AI Agents / Skills / Rules / Fine-Tuning.

**Product & lead:** Requirements gathering, scoping to an MVP, system integration design,
process automation, technical-to-business translation, mobile-first UX, bilingual (PL/EN)
product delivery, sprint planning, daily standups, client relations, budget discussions.

**People:** Mentoring, staff training & onboarding, workshop facilitation, conflict resolution,
team leadership (up to 12 people), translating technical language into plain human terms.

**Soft:** Fast learner, clear communicator, analytical problem solver, strong teammate,
relentless about continuous improvement (Kaizen). Yes -- also a professional rubber-duck.

Tech: Playwright, Cypress, Python, React, Angular, Java, Spring Boot, C#, .NET, Git, Bash,
Azure DevOps, CI/CD, E2E pipelines.

The rare role that combines engineering depth with product sense and client communication:

- Automated the entire manual client-onboarding process for a new product -- eliminated a
  category of work, not just sped it up.
- Ran penetration tests against AI features in production, found issues, shipped fixes.
- Built integrations between internal applications and third-party client systems.

  logic.

  Multi-Repo -- drove real adoption, not just awareness.

  migration itself.

## Selected projects

Each was designed, built, and shipped (or open-sourced) by one person unless noted.

- **CreativeShape** -- Start-up co-founded with a friend: NFC keychains for digital business
  cards. Friend handles the physical product; Ksawery owns everything online -- landing page,
  SEO, meta tags (main site + per-card `/w/*` subpages), and a full CMS for creating and
  editing cards. Heavy emphasis on collaborating with a non-technical co-founder: translating
  networking concepts, planning infrastructure, aligning on requirements, possibilities, and
  deadlines.
  Tech: React, Svelte, Drizzle, Tailwind CSS, Claude, Vercel.
  -> https://creativeshape.pl

- **Evenciki.pl** -- Event-planning platform built with university friends in one month:
  create an event, share a link, collect attendee responses. Mobile-first, bilingual (PL/EN).
  Ksawery handled team motivation, brand planning, scope definition, and out-of-scope
  trade-offs to ship the MVP as fast as possible.
  Tech: SvelteKit 5, NestJS, Drizzle ORM, PostgreSQL, TanStack Query, Tailwind, Bun.
  -> https://evenciki.pl

- **WizytowkaWeb (this portfolio)** -- The comet that flies through the DOM is a hand-built
  canvas animation system following a 1,500-point Catmull-Rom flight path -- built because a
  plain portfolio felt insufficient.
  Tech: React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vite, Canvas API.
  -> https://thelis3k.pl  |  https://github.com/TheLis3k/WebFrontEndShowcase

- **Restaurant Admin** -- Full-stack restaurant system: public reservation/menu site plus a
  role-based admin panel, JWT auth with rotating refresh tokens, invitation-based onboarding.
  The kind of auth most teams cut corners on -- done properly here. Built because the local
  pizzeria's only web presence was an old photo on Facebook.
  Tech: React, TypeScript, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, TanStack Query, Zustand, Docker.
  -> https://github.com/TheLis3k/WizytowkaSandbox

- **RyboKalkulator** -- Mobile app built for a friend working at a fish counter: add fish
  species with photos and trilingual names (3 languages), then price them fast. Designed for
  a low-end device (~1 GB RAM, old CPU), so lightweight and snappy was the whole brief --
  and it held up through a full busy season.
  Tech: Flutter, Dart, NoSQL DB, C++.
  -> https://github.com/TheLis3k/RyboKalkulator

- **How Much Is My Hot Wheels** -- Spring Boot REST API that scrapes eBay, Etsy, OLX, Vinted,
  and the Hot Wheels Wiki in parallel to aggregate live die-cast valuations. Built because it
  should exist. Public platform APIs were gatekept, so JSoup and Playwright scrapers were
  written instead.
  Tech: Java 21, Spring Boot, MongoDB, JSoup, Playwright, Docker.
  -> https://github.com/TheLis3k/how-much-is-my-hot-wheels

- **003-Expense-Tracker** -- First React project: interactive expense tracker with ChartJS
  visualisations, live currency conversion via API, and full RWD.
  Tech: React, JavaScript, CSS, ChartJS.
  -> https://github.com/TheLis3k/003-Expense-Tracker

- **FiveM Server DB Administration** -- Early project (age ~13-14): co-built a GTA 5 emulator
  server with friends, owned the MySQL database, handled bug reports, designed queries, and
  shipped schema modifications.
  Tech: MySQL, Excel, XML, phpMyAdmin.
